exercises.en: When the humidity is low, laundry dries quickly.
exercises.why: 낮다 ends in a consonant, so it takes 으면.

exercises.en: If the weather is cold, I'll rest at home.
exercises.why: 춥다 is ㅂ irregular, so ㅂ becomes 우 before 면.

exercises.en: Whenever I listen to music, I feel at ease.
exercises.why: 듣다 is ㄷ irregular, so ㄷ becomes ㄹ before 으면.

exercises.ko: 그때 열심히 ___ 시험을 잘 봤을 거예요.
exercises.en: If I had studied hard back then, I would have done well on the test.
exercises.why: For 'would have', the condition goes in the past: ~았/었으면.

exercises.en: If I had wings, I would fly in the sky.
exercises.why: 있다 stays 있다 in the plain form, so it becomes 있다면.

exercises.en: If you exercise every day, you will get healthier.
exercises.why: A vowel-stem verb takes ㄴ다면: 하다 becomes 한다면.

exercises.en: If I were the bride, I would be very happy.
exercises.why: With nouns 이다 becomes (이)라면, and 신부 ends in a vowel.

exercises.en: Please buy eggplant or hot peppers.
exercises.why: Between two nouns, 아니면 works like 'or'.

exercises.en: If you are tired, rest at home.
If there is a rainstorm tomorrow, I won't go out.
exercises.ko: 만약 내일 비바람이 불면 저는 밖에 안 나갈 거예요.

exercises.en: If I had known, I would have helped you.
If so, I will go alone.

reading.ko: 주말에 날씨가 좋으면 저는 빨래를 해요. 햇살이 강하면 빨래가 빨리 말라요. 하지만 습도가 높으면 빨래가 잘 안 말라요. 그러면 저는 기분이 안 좋아요. 만약 내일 비가 오면 빨래를 안 할 거예요. 친구에게 맛있는 음식을 대접할 거예요.
reading.en: When the weather is nice on the weekend, I do the laundry. When the sunlight is strong, the laundry dries quickly. But when the humidity is high, the laundry doesn't dry well. Then I'm in a bad mood. If it rains tomorrow, I won't do the laundry. I'll treat a friend to some delicious food.

questions.q: 날씨가 좋으면 이 사람은 뭘 해요?
내일 비가 오면 뭘 할 거예요?

exercises.en: Let's memorize the idioms together. (casual)
exercises.why: ~자 attaches directly to the stem and never takes 요.

exercises.en: Let's not tease that friend. (casual)
exercises.why: 'Let's not' is ~지 말자.

exercises.en: Let's postpone the meeting to tomorrow.
exercises.why: 하다 ends in a vowel, so it takes ㅂ시다.

exercises.en: Let's eat lunch together.
exercises.why: 먹다 ends in a consonant, so it takes 읍시다.

exercises.en: Let's all make gimbap together.
exercises.why: With ㄹ stems, the ㄹ drops before ㅂ시다.

exercises.en: Shall we walk in the park together on the weekend?
exercises.why: 걷다 is ㄷ irregular, so it becomes 걸을래요.

exercises.en: Could you pass this note to Minsu?
exercises.why: ~아/어 줄래요? makes a soft request.

exercises.en: I don't want to watch this movie.
exercises.why: As a statement, ~ㄹ래요 says what I want to do.

exercises.en: Let's go to the library together. (casual)
Let's start the training tomorrow.
What do you want to eat for dinner?
Could you turn on the TV?

reading.ko: 민수: 지수야, 주말에 뭐 할래? 지수: 날씨가 좋으면 공원에 가자. 민수: 좋아. 같이 김밥을 만들자. 지수: 그런데 나는 토요일에 연수가 있어. 일요일에 갈래? 민수: 그래, 일요일에 가자. 지수: 그럼 열한 시에 우리 집 앞에서 만나자.
reading.en: Minsu: Jisu, what do you want to do this weekend? Jisu: If the weather is nice, let's go to the park. Minsu: Sounds good. Let's make gimbap together. Jisu: But I have training on Saturday. Do you want to go on Sunday? Minsu: OK, let's go on Sunday. Jisu: Then let's meet in front of my house at eleven.

exercises.en: I can sing Korean songs.
exercises.why: 부르다 ends in a vowel, so it takes ㄹ before 수.

exercises.en: My leg hurts, so I can't walk for long.
exercises.why: 걷다 is ㄷ irregular, so it becomes 걸을.

exercises.en: You can apply this medicine to your hands.
exercises.why: 바르다 ends in a vowel, so it simply takes ㄹ.

exercises.en: I can make kimchi.
exercises.why: ㄹ stems take nothing extra: 만들 수 있어요.

exercises.ko: 어제는 너무 바빠서 점심을 먹을 수 ___.
exercises.en: Yesterday I was so busy that I couldn't eat lunch.
exercises.why: Only 없다 changes for tense, so the past is 없었어요.

exercises.en: I'll probably be able to come early tomorrow.
exercises.why: For the future, put 있다 in the future: 있을 거예요.

exercises.ko: 이 문제는 너무 어려워서 혼자 풀 수___ 없어요.
exercises.en: This problem is so hard that I just can't solve it alone.
exercises.why: 수 ends in a vowel, so the emphatic particle is 가.

exercises.ko: 숙제를 할 때 이 사전을 참고___ 수 있어요.
exercises.en: When you do your homework, you can refer to this dictionary.
exercises.why: 하다 becomes 할 before 수 있다.

exercises.en: Can you speak Japanese?
I couldn't go to the party yesterday.
If the deadline passes, you can't get a refund.
exercises.ko: 기한이 지나면 환불을 받을 수 없어요.

exercises.en: This road is slippery, so you can't ride a bike.
exercises.ko: 이 길은 미끄러워서 자전거를 탈 수 없어요.

reading.ko: 오늘 아침에 첫눈이 왔어요. 길이 아주 미끄러웠어요. 그래서 저는 빨리 걸을 수 없었어요. 버스도 빨리 올 수 없었어요. 저는 회사에 늦게 도착했어요. 내일은 눈이 안 오면 일찍 갈 수 있을 거예요.
reading.en: This morning the first snow fell. The roads were very slippery. So I couldn't walk fast. The bus couldn't come quickly either. I arrived at work late. Tomorrow, if it doesn't snow, I'll probably be able to go early.

exercises.en: I have to review this plan before the meeting.
exercises.why: 하다 verbs become 해야 before 하다/되다.

exercises.ko: 내일 시험이 있어서 오늘 일찍 ___ 해요.
exercises.en: I have a test tomorrow, so I have to go to bed early today.
exercises.why: 자다 ends in ㅏ, so 아야 contracts to 자야.

exercises.en: You have to listen carefully to what the teacher says.
exercises.why: 듣다 is ㄷ irregular, so it becomes 들어야.

exercises.en: Last week I had to go to the office early every day.
exercises.why: Only the final 하다 changes for tense: 가야 했어요.

exercises.en: I need a new computer.
exercises.why: 필요하다 is an adjective, so the needed thing takes 이/가, and 컴퓨터 ends in a vowel.

exercises.en: There's no need to take an umbrella today.
exercises.why: ~ㄹ/을 필요가 없다 means there is no need to.

exercises.en: It's already ten o'clock. I'd better go home now.
exercises.why: ~아/어야겠다 means 'I'd better' after realizing something.

exercises.en: If you're sick, you should go to the hospital, of course.
exercises.why: In speech, ~아/어야죠 means 'of course you should'.

exercises.en: We have to connect these two computers.
I need a new phone.
If you want to succeed, you have to work hard.
There's no need to buy a new fence.

reading.ko: 다음 주에 시험이 있어요. 그래서 이번 주에는 공부를 많이 해야 돼요. 그런데 요즘 시력이 나빠져서 화면이 잘 안 보여요. 안경이 필요해요. 내일 안경을 사러 가야겠어요. 친구가 좋은 안경 가게를 알고 있어요. 그래서 걱정할 필요가 없어요.
reading.en: I have a test next week. So I have to study a lot this week. But lately my eyesight has gotten worse, so I can't see the screen well. I need glasses. I'd better go buy glasses tomorrow. My friend knows a good glasses shop. So there's no need to worry.

questions.a: 친구가 좋은 안경 가게를 알고 있어요.

exercises.en: This apartment is expensive, but it's very spacious.
exercises.why: ~지만 attaches straight to the stem to show contrast.

exercises.en: I was very sick yesterday, but today I'm okay.
exercises.why: For a past contrast, add ~지만 after 았/었: 아팠지만.

exercises.en: That person is a student, but has a lot of money.
exercises.why: 학생 ends in a consonant, so 이다 + 지만 is 이지만.

exercises.en: That movie was long, but it was fun.
exercises.why: The movie was long in the past, so use 길었지만.

exercises.en: The wound is big, but it doesn't hurt much.
exercises.why: ~지만 attaches to the stem with no change: 크지만.

exercises.en: It will probably be cold tomorrow, but I'll go exercise.
exercises.why: For a guess about the future, use ~겠지만.

exercises.en: I logged in, but the screen doesn't change.
exercises.why: The login already happened, so use the past 했지만.

exercises.ko: 저는 그 사람이 좋아요. ___ 결혼은 안 할 거예요.
exercises.en: I like that person. However, I won't marry them.
exercises.why: 그렇지만 starts a sentence meaning 'however'.

exercises.en: I wanted to participate, but I didn't have time.
The sunlight is warm, but the wind is cold.
However, I can't go today.
exercises.ko: 그렇지만 저는 오늘 갈 수 없어요.

exercises.en: I'm sorry, but I can't help you.

reading.ko: 우리 아파트는 작지만 아주 깨끗해요. 아파트 앞에는 넓은 잔디가 있어요. 잔디는 예쁘지만 들어갈 수 없어요. 경비 아저씨는 엄격하시지만 친절하세요. 어제 우리 강아지가 잔디에 들어갔어요. 아저씨는 소리를 지르셨지만 강아지를 보고 웃으셨어요.
reading.en: Our apartment is small but very clean. In front of the apartment there is a wide lawn. The lawn is pretty, but you can't go on it. The security guard is strict but kind. Yesterday our puppy went onto the lawn. The guard shouted, but then he saw the puppy and laughed.

exercises.en: Even if it rains, I'll go for a walk.
exercises.why: 오다 + 아도 contracts to 와도.

exercises.en: No matter how much I exercise, I don't lose weight.
exercises.why: 아무리 goes with ~아/어도, and 하다 becomes 해도.

exercises.en: At this restaurant, whatever you eat is delicious.
exercises.why: 뭘 + ~아/어도 means 'whatever', and 먹다 takes 어도.

exercises.en: Even if it's cold, I open the window.
exercises.why: 춥다 is ㅂ irregular, so it becomes 추워도.

exercises.en: No matter how fast the bus is, we will be late.
exercises.why: 빠르다 is 르 irregular, so it becomes 빨라도.

exercises.ko: 비싼 보석___ 저는 안 받을 거예요.
exercises.en: Even if it's an expensive jewel, I won't accept it.
exercises.why: 보석 ends in a consonant, so 이다 becomes 이어도.

exercises.ko: 그 사람이 건축가___ 이 집은 지을 수 없을 거예요.
exercises.en: Even if that person is an architect, they won't be able to build this house.
exercises.why: 건축가 ends in a vowel, so 이어도 shortens to 여도.

exercises.ko: 오늘은 비가 많이 와요. ___ 박람회에 갈 거예요.
exercises.en: It's raining a lot today. Even so, I'll go to the fair.
exercises.why: 그래도 means 'even so'.

exercises.en: Even if I'm busy, I call my mom every day.
No matter how sweet it is, I don't like cake.
exercises.ko: 아무리 달콤해도 저는 케이크를 안 좋아해요.

exercises.en: Even on weekends, I can't sleep late.
It's expensive. Even so, I want to buy it.

reading.ko: 우리 가족은 매년 여름에 호숫가에 가요. 비가 와도 우리는 꼭 가요. 작년에는 태풍이 왔어요. 그래도 우리는 호숫가에 갔어요. 거기는 아무리 더워도 바람이 시원해요. 호수에는 새끼 오리가 많아요. 새끼 오리는 아무리 봐도 귀여워요.
reading.en: My family goes to the lakeside every summer. Even if it rains, we always go. Last year a typhoon came. Even so, we went to the lakeside. No matter how hot it is there, the wind is cool. There are many ducklings on the lake. No matter how often I look at them, the ducklings are cute.

questions.q: 태풍이 왔지만 이 가족은 어떻게 했어요?

exercises.en: May I use this computer?
exercises.why: 쓰다 is ㅡ irregular, so 쓰 + 어도 becomes 써도.

exercises.en: May I borrow this pen?
exercises.why: 빌리 + 어도 contracts to 빌려도.

exercises.en: Is it okay if I listen to music?
exercises.why: 듣다 is ㄷ irregular, so it becomes 들어도.

exercises.en: You can go to bed early today.
exercises.why: ~아/어도 좋다 gives permission, and 자 + 아도 is 자도.

exercises.en: You don't have to do your homework today.
exercises.why: 안 + ~아/어도 되다 means 'you don't have to'.

exercises.en: You don't have to wear a suit.
exercises.why: ~지 않아도 되다 means 'you don't have to'.

exercises.en: The internet isn't working well.
exercises.why: 되다 here means 'to work', and 되어요 contracts to 돼요.

exercises.en: The rice is ready.
exercises.why: 되다 can mean 'to be done', and 되었어요 contracts to 됐어요.

exercises.en: May I open this box?
You don't have to come tomorrow.
Is it okay if I call you tonight?
You don't have to have a license.

reading.ko: 오늘 학교에서 탁구 시합이 있었어요. 시합 전에 감독관님이 규정을 설명해 주셨어요. 시합 중에 물을 마셔도 돼요. 그리고 꼭 이기지 않아도 돼요. 저는 시합에서 이기지 못했지만 정말 재미있었어요. 다음 시합에도 꼭 참가할 거예요.
reading.en: Today there was a table tennis match at school. Before the match, the supervisor explained the rules. You may drink water during the match. And you don't have to win. I couldn't win the match, but it was really fun. I'll definitely take part in the next match too.

exercises.en: I'm scheduled to go to Jeju Island next week.
exercises.why: 예정 is described with the future modifier ㄹ/을.

exercises.en: They plan to build a big airport on that island.
exercises.why: 짓다 is ㅅ irregular, so the ㅅ drops: 지을.

exercises.en: The meeting is scheduled to end at two.
exercises.why: 예정 ends in a consonant, so 이다 becomes 이에요.

exercises.en: I have plans to become a vegetarian.
exercises.why: 계획 ends in a consonant and is followed by 있다, so it takes 이.

exercises.en: I have no plans to move this year.
exercises.why: Having no plans is ~ㄹ/을 계획이 없다.

exercises.en: I am ready to take the test now.
exercises.why: 준비가 됐어요 means the preparation is done: 'I'm ready'.

exercises.en: I'm getting ready to go out now.
exercises.why: With the action verb 하다, 준비 takes the object particle, and it ends in a vowel.

exercises.en: Mom is getting ready to grill the meat.
exercises.why: 굽다 (to grill) is ㅂ irregular, so it becomes 구울.

exercises.en: The test is scheduled to start at nine.
Do you have plans to quit your job?
Are you ready to leave?
Hurry up and get ready to eat.

reading.ko: 저는 다음 달에 친구들과 작은 섬에 갈 예정이에요. 섬에서 삼 일 동안 있을 계획이에요. 저는 채식주의자라서 고기를 안 먹어요. 그래서 친구들이 고기를 구우면 저는 야채를 구울 거예요. 섬에서 복숭아하고 참외도 먹을 계획이 있어요. 지금 여행 갈 준비를 하고 있어요. 하지만 아직 준비가 다 안 됐어요.
reading.en: Next month I'm scheduled to go to a small island with my friends. We plan to stay on the island for three days. I'm a vegetarian, so I don't eat meat. So when my friends grill meat, I'll grill vegetables. We also plan to eat peaches and oriental melons on the island. I'm getting ready for the trip now. But I'm not completely ready yet.

questions.q: 이 사람은 다음 달에 어디에 갈 예정이에요?
이 사람은 왜 고기를 안 먹어요?
